## The order's FIRST instruction is a falsification, ⛔ not an edit

The dev was told to re-take the premise itself before touching the file, with both legs in one run: the SUBJECT (spec built from objectstack `main`, injected the way `scripts/spec-main-shape-gate.mjs inject` does it) must report the `TS2322` at line 76 and nothing else in `@object-ui/react`; the CONTROL (the published pin the lockfile resolves, `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0`) must report **zero**. A non-zero control, or a subject set this card does not name, is a STOP — the repair shape described here would then be aimed at the wrong thing.

⚠️ One known hazard is named in the order: `scripts/spec-main-shape-gate.mjs` lives on PR #9877's branch, ⛔ not on `main`. The dev was told to read it from there and ⛔ not to reconstruct the injection by guess; if it cannot reproduce the injection at all, it must say so and declare that the gate leg was NOT run rather than let a hand-typed type-check stand in for it silently.

## The two constraints that decide the repair

1. ⛔ **Do NOT delete the `view` member**, and ⛔ do not weaken either assertion in the row it feeds. That row is a tombstone BEHAVIOUR pin, and it is the only row in the file that can fail if the substitution comes back.
2. The `SpecAuthoredInput<typeof NavigationConfigSchema>` annotation **survives** — it IS the objectui#4550 type pin. It just has to author a key the spec still declares.

The precedent to copy rather than invent is named: `packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/gridNavigationMembers-8071.test.tsx:93` already types a legacy body as `Record<string, unknown>` and keeps both rows while compiling clean against main's spec.

The order also requires the file's header to be brought back into agreement with what the file then does — «the fixture keeps its `view` member on purpose» stays true but stops being complete once the member is carried as a stored body rather than as authored metadata.

## Not re-opened

Ruling **A** on #9874 (director seat, summon #25, 2026-09-20T09:04Z) and the spec's `retiredKey` tombstone are both quoted into the order as standing constraints: ⛔ no re-declaration, ⛔ no deprecated alias, ⛔ no spec-side workaround.

## Landing is this seat's

The dev was told the PR stays **DRAFT**: ⛔ no label, ⛔ no ready flip, ⛔ no auto-merge. It was also told ⛔ no MCP GitHub write tool, and to list every API write it makes.

And the header now carries the sentence that stops the regression: 「⛔ The member may not go back inside a `SpecAuthoredInput` literal: the spec types the retired key `never`」. ⭐ That is the difference between a fix and a fix that survives.

My order allowed a declared fallback if the injection could not be reproduced. | subject, after | built from `main` | `OPT of z.ZodNever` | **0** |

⇒ ⭐ the four corners are the whole claim: it now compiles against `main` **and** still compiles against the pin, so it is ⛔ not「compiles against main because it stopped compiling against everything」.

The second file.** ⭐ **A — keep it.** The card's own acceptance line delegated the changeset to the repo's gate («confirm with the repo's own gate, ⛔ not from memory»), the gate went red on the test-only diff and named the empty-frontmatter form as 「the explicit exemption and a complete answer to this gate」. ⇒ that file is the gate's answer, ⛔ not a widening: it releases nothing and names no package. Stopping as blocked would have been obeying the surface line over the acceptance line that governs it. ⭐ Flagging it rather than treating it as licence to widen is exactly right.

**2. The commit trailers.** ⭐ **A — model-free is correct, and not merely the lesser evil.** The standing instruction is explicit that no model identifier goes into a commit message, PR title or body, or any other artefact pushed to a repository — that is a rule about repository artefacts, and it governs here. ⛔ Nothing to re-write, and a force-push would have been forbidden regardless.
